overview:
The AI customer-support market is in a consolidation-and-collision phase. Frontier labs (OpenAI's Presence, Anthropic's Claude Cowork/Tag) are moving down-market into the exact deployed-agent territory Decagon, Sierra, Parloa and Cresta occupy, while incumbent SaaS platforms are buying their way into AI-native support rather than building it — most visibly Salesforce's ~$3.6B acquisition of Fin (formerly Intercom), confirmed by Salesforce's own press release and TechCrunch, and Sierra's acquisition of TakeOff. At the same time, a wall of cheap, capable open-source and Chinese models (DeepSeek V4 Pro, Alibaba's Qwen 3.8, Moonshot's Kimi K3) keeps compressing the cost of the underlying intelligence, which matters directly to margin structure for every agent vendor, Decagon included.

The podcast evidence adds a useful mindshare data point: Decagon's founders used their a16z appearance ('How Enterprise AI Really Gets Deployed') to make an architectural and philosophical statement — running roughly 90% of platform workflows on fine-tuned open-source models and explicitly rejecting the forward-deployed-engineer (FDE) staffing model that Sierra, OpenAI Presence and most systems-integrator-style competitors lean on. That framing is now showing up across Newcomer, StartupHub and Decagon's own blog as a coherent narrative: product-led deployment versus headcount-heavy deployment. It's a real fork in go-to-market philosophy at the exact moment OpenAI chose to launch Presence as a boots-on-the-ground, FDE-led, no-self-serve-tier product starting around $10M in enterprise contracts.

Meanwhile the market's two biggest 'proof' stories are pulling in opposite directions. Salesforce touts Agentforce crossing $1B ARR and $2.7M closed for SaaStr, but KeyBanc, Morgan Stanley and multiple analyst downgrades openly question whether that revenue reflects real production usage versus land-grab bundling — a gap Forethought's own research reinforces by finding AI adoption in CX near 70% but only 2% of programs meeting a real 'Center of Excellence' bar. That gap between headline traction and operational maturity is exactly where a product built for fast, verifiable resolution (not pilots) can win competitive displacements over the next several quarters.

themes.name: Frontier labs go direct-to-enterprise
themes.description: OpenAI's Presence and Anthropic's Claude Cowork/Tag/Teams integration move the model providers from API supplier to deployed-agent operator, directly overlapping Decagon's core wedge. Both are choosing consulting-style, engineer-led rollouts rather than self-serve products, which slows their reach into mid-market but raises the stakes at the largest logos.

evidence.label: OpenAI launches Presence, an enterprise platform for voice/chat agents with BBVA, SoftBank, IAG as early customers; OpenAI's own support line resolves 75% of issues on it
Presence has no self-serve tier or public pricing; deployments run through OpenAI's Forward Deployed Engineers, entry point reportedly ~$10M
Anthropic argues most 'agents' in production are glorified chatbots, positioning itself as the maturity-focused alternative
HubSpot stock fell 12.7% with analysts pointing to OpenAI's new customer-facing agent push

themes.name: Incumbents buy their way in, but the ROI story splits analysts
themes.description: Salesforce's ~$3.6B acquisition of Fin (formerly Intercom) confirms that incumbents now prefer buying proven AI-native support technology over building it internally, while Sierra's acquisition of TakeOff shows even AI-native leaders are rolling up point solutions. Yet Salesforce's own Agentforce, despite crossing $1B ARR, faces open skepticism from KeyBanc and Morgan Stanley about real customer traction versus bundled/land-grab revenue.

evidence.label: Salesforce signs definitive agreement to acquire Fin (formerly Intercom) for ~$3.6B, folding it into Agentforce
Sierra acquires TakeOff, a long-horizon AI agent platform that had scaled to nearly $10M ARR
Agentforce crosses $1B ARR, but KeyBanc says Agentforce 'as a product, just isn't there' and cites weak customer traction
Morgan Stanley: Agentforce performing well operationally but adoption hasn't driven a measurable organic-growth inflection

themes.name: Open-source and Chinese model price collapse rewrites unit economics
themes.description: DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Moonshot's Kimi are each getting compared to a 'DeepSeek moment,' pushing frontier-level reasoning and voice capability down toward commodity pricing. This directly affects the margin structure every agent vendor runs on, and gives ammunition to open-source-first architectures like Decagon's.

evidence.label: DeepSeek ships V4 Pro as its flagship model leaves preview, closing in on frontier-tier performance at a fraction of the price
Alibaba's Qwen 3.8 previewed as 'second only to Fable 5,' expanding cost-effective near-frontier options
Decagon founders tell a16z's podcast the platform runs ~90% of workflows on fine-tuned open-source models
Samsung in talks for a €1B stake in Mistral, backing a European open-model alternative to closed APIs

themes.name: Outcome-based, pay-per-resolution pricing becomes the default ask
themes.description: Sierra's Horizon agents and Salesforce's Agentforce Help Agent both moved to pay-for-results/pay-per-resolution pricing instead of seats or tokens, and Bessemer's 'durable monetization' piece frames this as the industry-wide answer to the AI pricing puzzle. Buyers are now trained to expect resolution-based commercial terms, not subscriptions.

evidence.label: Sierra launches Horizon agents using outcomes-based, pay-for-results pricing rather than token consumption
Salesforce's Agentforce Help Agent deploys in minutes and only charges for resolutions
The Futurum Group questions whether enterprises will trust pay-per-resolution pricing at scale
Bessemer's 'durable monetization' piece features Ada among founders describing the shift to outcome-based AI pricing

themes.name: Voice becomes the primary battleground
themes.description: Nearly every major player shipped a voice announcement in the last 90 days — Sierra's Voice Personas and IVR navigation, OpenAI's GPT-Live, ElevenLabs' $22B valuation and celebrity-voice licensing, Parloa's guardrails and SAP certification, PolyAI's new conversation model, and ByteDance's SeedRealtime. Voice is where latency, naturalness and telephony integration are becoming the real differentiators, not just chat resolution rates.

evidence.label: ElevenLabs' valuation doubles to $22B on synthetic-voice demand
OpenAI ships GPT-Live, a turnless low-latency speech architecture for continuous voice interaction
Sierra launches Voice Personas and teaches agents to navigate janky IVR systems out of the box
ByteDance launches SeedRealtime, a native full-duplex audio-video model, making the realtime voice race multi-polar
Decagon ships Decagon Voice, its enterprise-grade voice agent product

themes.name: Product-led deployment vs. forward-deployed-engineer armies
themes.description: Decagon is explicitly positioning against the forward-deployed-engineer (FDE) model that Sierra and now OpenAI Presence lean on, arguing product-led tooling scales better than headcount-heavy consulting engagements. Newcomer's reporting on Decagon crossing $100M ARR while rejecting the FDE model, plus its a16z podcast appearance, frame this as a real strategic fork rather than just marketing.

evidence.label: Newcomer reports Decagon passed $100M ARR while deliberately rejecting the forward-deployed-engineer model rivals lean on
StartupHub profiles Decagon's CTO on why the company builds product-led deployment tooling instead of an FDE army
OpenAI Presence launches with no self-serve tier — deployments led entirely by OpenAI's Forward Deployed Engineers
Decagon announces Agent Deployment Engineering, its own answer to the FDE debate built into the product organization

convergence: Everyone is converging on the same rectangle of enterprise budget from different starting points: frontier labs (OpenAI, Anthropic) are moving down from raw model APIs into managed, governed agent deployment; horizontal CRM/CCaaS incumbents (Salesforce, and now Fin under its wing) are buying finished AI-native support products instead of building them; BPOs and contact-center operators (Firstsource+Cresta, TTEC+Salesforce, SoftBank+Sierra) are becoming distribution partners rather than just labor providers; voice specialists (ElevenLabs, PolyAI, Parloa) are getting embedded into every layer via partnerships (IBM, TELUS, SAP); and no-code aggregators (Relevance AI) are commoditizing templated agents at the low end. The collision point is the mid-market-to-enterprise CX budget, where pricing is converging on outcome/resolution-based models and deployment speed is converging on 'product-led self-serve' versus 'FDE-heavy consulting' as the two competing playbooks — with open-source and Chinese model price cuts quietly subsidizing all of it by compressing the cost of the underlying intelligence layer.

predictions.claim: OpenAI Presence will land a handful of marquee logos (in the BBVA/SoftBank/IAG mold) but will not meaningfully dent Decagon or Sierra's core pipeline in the next two quarters because of its consulting-priced, non-self-serve model.
predictions.rationale: Presence launched with no public pricing, no self-serve tier, and an estimated ~$10M enterprise entry point delivered via Forward Deployed Engineers, which limits its addressable market to the very largest accounts.

predictions.claim: At least one more mid-size CX AI vendor (in the size class of Parloa, Cresta or a Relevance AI-style player) will be acquired by a CRM/CCaaS incumbent by end of 2026, following the Salesforce-Fin pattern.
predictions.rationale: Salesforce's ~$3.6B Fin deal was explicitly framed as one of three $3B+ B2B acquisitions in 30 days built around buying AI-native customer data and agents rather than building them, signaling an active incumbent shopping spree.

predictions.claim: Outcome-based / pay-per-resolution pricing will become the majority commercial model offered on new enterprise agent RFPs within the next 12 months, forcing every vendor including Decagon to publish or default to resolution-based terms.
predictions.rationale: Sierra's Horizon agents, Salesforce's Agentforce Help Agent, and Bessemer's founder roundtable all independently converged on outcome-based pricing as the answer to enterprise AI's monetization puzzle within the same quarter.

predictions.claim: Voice will overtake chat as the primary area of vendor investment and buyer evaluation through 2027, as latency and TTS quality gaps close.
predictions.rationale: In just the last 90 days nearly every major player — Sierra, OpenAI, ElevenLabs, Parloa, PolyAI, ByteDance and Decagon itself — shipped a distinct voice product or model, indicating investment is concentrating there.

predictions.claim: Salesforce's Agentforce will keep generating analyst skepticism (further downgrades or 'proof gap' commentary) even as its headline ARR keeps climbing, creating openings for Decagon to win competitive displacements in accounts that tried Agentforce first.
predictions.rationale: KeyBanc, Morgan Stanley and multiple outlets have already flagged a gap between Agentforce's reported ARR growth and demonstrated customer traction, and Salesforce has also seen a string of Agentforce engineering-leadership departures.
